dealNotes: Multiyear agreement. Vanderbilt Health becomes Official Healthcare Provider of the Tennessee Titans and Nissan Stadium. Training facility renamed Vanderbilt Health Football Center. Vanderbilt LifeFlight Event Medicine provides first aid and emergency medical services for all stadium events. As a founding Cornerstone Sponsor of the new $2.1B Nissan Stadium (opening 2027), VUMC receives a branded family zone named the Monroe Carell Jr. Children's Hospital at Vanderbilt Terrace, a Vanderbilt Health entry gate, and permanent signage inside the 60,000-capacity stadium bowl. Partnership includes community initiatives centered on Monroe Carell Jr. Children's Hospital and youth sports. Replaces Ascension Saint Thomas, which ended its partnership effective March 1, 2026.

financials.source: Form 990 FY2024 via ProPublica Nonprofit Explorer (EIN 35-2528741); VUMC Continuing Disclosure Report; Becker's Hospital Review (operating income and margin from disclosure report data). Total revenue of $7,706,035,528 per Form 990. Operating income of $168.3M on ~$7.6B operating revenue per disclosure report (2.2% margin), up from $51.7M (0.8% margin) in FY2023. Net income of $320.8M includes $67M Medicare 340B settlement and $83M in one-time state-directed payments. FY2025 interim (nine months ended March 31, 2025): operating revenue $6,192M (+11% YoY), income from operations $120.3M, operating margin 1.9%, total assets $7,241,679,000. VUMC separated from Vanderbilt University in April 2016 as an independent nonprofit; these figures are VUMC-only, not the university.

balanceSheetWealth.investmentPortfolioSource: VUMC Consolidated Balance Sheet as of June 30, 2024 — noncurrent investments of $1,073,228 thousand, up from $932,952 thousand at June 30, 2023. Separately, noncurrent investments limited as to use totaled $209,718 thousand. Total noncurrent investment-related assets approximately $1.28B. FY2023 audited statements noted VUMC has $2,447.6M of financial assets available within one year, including unrestricted investments of $1,037.9M.
balanceSheetWealth.endowmentSource: VUMC permanent endowment funds of $111.4M per state disclosure note. This is VUMC's own endowment, separate from Vanderbilt University's ~$10.9B endowment (FY2025). The university and medical center maintain separate balance sheets since the April 2016 separation.
balanceSheetWealth.notes: VUMC manages all investments, including endowments, in various investment pools. Net assets without donor restrictions were $2,117,322,000 and net assets with donor restrictions were $344,414,000 as of June 30, 2024. Total net assets grew from $2,113,555,000 (FY2023) to $2,461,736,000 (FY2024). As of March 31, 2025 (interim), total assets had grown to $7,241,679,000, driven in part by the $600M Tennova Healthcare-Clarksville acquisition. VUMC's investment portfolio is modest compared to the largest health systems but represents substantial accumulated nonprofit wealth for a single-market academic medical center.

communityBenefit.source: VUMC news release (March 26, 2025): $952 million in charity care, community benefits and other unrecovered costs for FY2024. Includes costs directly supporting patients through financial assistance, unreimbursed TennCare/Medicaid costs, community health improvement grants, and investments in medical research and education. Broader definition claims more than $1B in total community benefit and investment. Percentage calculated against FY2024 Form 990 total revenue of $7,706,035,528. Combined Vanderbilt University and VUMC economic impact on Nashville and Tennessee: $22.13B from 2019-2024. Schedule H community benefit breakdown not extracted from Form 990 filing.

taxAdvantage.notes: VUMC is a 501(c)(3) tax-exempt organization (EIN 35-2528741, tax-exempt since 2015 following April 2016 separation from Vanderbilt University). Tennessee has no state income tax on wages, but VUMC benefits from federal income tax exemption, property tax exemption on its Nashville/Davidson County campus and satellite facilities, and the ability to issue tax-exempt revenue bonds through the HEFB. Multiple bond series outstanding through Nashville's Health and Educational Facilities Board, with over $1B in new issuance in 2026 alone. No PILOT (payment in lieu of taxes) agreement found in Nashville Metro Council records.

layoffs.notes: Initial round of cost reductions: hiring freeze for most research and administrative positions, some positions eliminated. Part of $250M cost-cutting effort in response to federal funding reductions.

Up to 650 employees laid off, largely research, administration and support roles (less than 2% of total workforce). Tennessee WARN notice filed for 615 workers with effective date of April 8, 2025. Combined with earlier cuts as part of $300M+ operating cost reduction. Driven by federal budgetary actions related to government-sponsored research and patient care, including proposed NIH funding cuts and Medicaid changes. Clinical positions largely unaffected. Laid-off employees received severance packages and outplacement assistance.
layoffs.source: FierceHealthcare; WPLN Nashville; Tennessee Lookout; WSMV Nashville; Nashville Banner; HealthLeaders Media; Tennessee Department of Labor WARN notice tracker (615 workers); Kadoa layoff tracker

keyRiskFactors: Historically thin operating margins — 2.2% in FY2024, improved from 0.8% in FY2023 but partly driven by one-time items ($67M Medicare 340B settlement + $83M state-directed payments)
Heavy reliance on federal funding — $300M+ in budget cuts triggered by proposed NIH and Medicaid reductions, leading to 650 layoffs in 2025
Significant debt growth — multiple new bond series since 2016 separation, including $1.09B offering in 2026 and $450M Series 2024A
$600M acquisition of Tennova Healthcare-Clarksville adds integration risk and leverage
Single-market concentration in Middle Tennessee unlike diversified multi-state systems
CEO transition underway — Balser retiring December 2026, successor from University of Michigan starting January 2027
creditRating.source: Moody's A3 with Stable outlook affirmed on approximately $926M of VUMC outstanding bonds (Becker's Hospital Review, circa 2017). S&P 'A' rating inferred from Piper Sandler Weekly Healthcare Market Update April 6, 2026 listing VUMC offering as 'NR/A/A' (interpreted as not rated by one agency / A by S&P / A by another). Current ratings may differ; VUMC's standalone credit profile is significantly lower than Vanderbilt University's ratings (Fitch AAA, S&P AAA, Moody's Aa1) because the entities separated in 2016. No 2024-2025 rating actions found for VUMC specifically in search results.

program340B.notes: Pioneer Institute Tennessee report lists VUMC with 259 contract pharmacies, of which 62 (24%) are located outside Tennessee. A 2021 InvestigateTV/KHN investigation reported VUMC grew from zero contract pharmacies in 2010 to approximately 300, making it one of the top hospitals nationally for 340B contract pharmacy growth after federal rules changed. Contract pharmacies include Walgreens, CVS, Accredo, and others stretching from Tennessee to California. VUMC describes these as 'Multiple Contract Pharmacies' serving VUMC patients. Revenue from the 340B program supports medication assistance, home infusion medications, and a student-run health clinic pharmacy program. In a 2021 amicus brief, VUMC reported losing $12.4M in 340B savings from a Medicare reimbursement cut. FDLI (Food and Drug Law Institute) article lists VUMC with a fair share deficit of -$157M based on author's methodology. In FY2024, VUMC received a $67M Medicare 340B settlement payment.
program340B.source: Pioneer Institute Tennessee 340B report (2025); InvestigateTV/KHN (2021); VUMC Terminology Document (January 2025); FDLI (2022); Bangor Daily News; VUMC amicus brief (2021); 340breform.org

legalIssues.description: Two patients filed a class-action lawsuit against VUMC alleging the hospital disclosed protected health information of 106 transgender patients to the Tennessee Attorney General's office without adequate safeguards. Plaintiffs allege VUMC violated HIPAA and failed to protect personal health information. VUMC maintains it was legally obligated to comply with the AG's investigative subpoena. The AG's office stated its investigation focused on medical billing fraud related to the hospital's transgender care program. A separate federal civil rights investigation was opened in August 2023.
legalIssues.status: In June 2024, a U.S. Senate Finance Committee report concluded VUMC did not do enough to protect the privacy of its transgender patients. Case status as of October 2026 not confirmed from available search results.
legalIssues.source: WPLN Nashville; Becker's Hospital Review; HIPAA Journal; KFF Health News; NewsChannel 5 Nashville; U.S. Senate Finance Committee

legalIssues.description: VUMC paid $6.5 million to resolve a whistleblower False Claims Act lawsuit alleging improper billing for attending physician services and unnecessary anesthesia. The lawsuit was filed under seal in 2011 by three former VUMC anesthesiologists.
legalIssues.status: Settled. VUMC stated the settlement was to avoid the cost of litigation and strongly disputed the allegations.
legalIssues.source: Becker's Hospital Review; The Edu Ledger
